clue.text: Sly peep around catches one in fit condition

indicators.note: catches means the jumbled letters hold another piece inside them
around suggests the letters of sly peep are turned about and rearranged

parts.note: one is the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: A sneaky voyeur takes a peek at someone who happens to be in good physical shape.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fit' looks like 'healthy' in the surface, but the definition reads it as a seizure: a condition marked by fits.
explanation.definitionFit: The neurological disorder is characterised by recurrent seizures, which are commonly called fits.

clue.text: Keep tabs on vacuous liars — they're slippery

parts.note: a tab is slang for an ecstasy tablet, abbreviated E; two tabs give two of them

indicators.note: vacuous means empty, so only the outside letters of liars remain

explanation.surface: Someone is told to keep an eye on dishonest people who cannot be pinned down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Keep tabs on' reads as 'monitor', but here 'tabs' is drug slang: an E is an ecstasy tablet, so two tabs give EE. 'Keep' and 'on' are link words.
explanation.definitionFit: These fish have smooth, mucus-coated skin, making them proverbially hard to hold.

clue.text: State protected in biowarfare

indicators.note: protected in means the letters sit sheltered within the word biowarfare

explanation.surface: A government is shielded by a programme of germ warfare.
explanation.definitionFit: It is one of the fifty constituent states of the USA, in the Midwest.

clue.text: Stood up on end of bride's dress

indicators.note: on in a down clue puts the first piece above the second
up in a down clue means the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: stood in the sense of endured or tolerated, past participle borne

indicators.note: end of picks the final letter of bride's

explanation.surface: A groom is left standing at the altar on the bride's last word about her gown.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stood' must be read as 'put up with', giving BORNE, which 'up' turns into ENROB.
explanation.definitionFit: To clothe someone in a robe or gown is to dress them, a formal verb.

clue.text: They restore millions pocketed by retail crew

indicators.note: pocketed by means the abbreviation is held inside the word for retail

parts.note: to retail is to sell goods, so retail gives selling
M is the standard abbreviation for million(s)
salts are sailors, the crew of a ship

explanation.surface: A shop's staff are caught taking millions, but the cash is put back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pocketed by' puts M inside SELLING. 'crew' sounds collective, but old sailors are called salts, as in 'old salt'.
explanation.definitionFit: Ammonium carbonate preparations were sniffed to revive someone who had fainted, bringing them round.

clue.text: Latitude given by king, subject admits

indicators.note: admits means the word for subject lets the king's letter in

parts.note: a subject of discussion is a topic
R is the abbreviation for king, from Latin rex

explanation.surface: A monarch grants freedom, and one of his subjects concedes it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Latitude' looks like 'freedom' but is the geographical sense: a line of latitude.
explanation.definitionFit: The tropics of Cancer and Capricorn are specific parallels north and south of the equator.

clue.text: Problem clues like this will be good after exercise

parts.note: rub means a problem, as in Hamlet's 'there's the rub'
this clue is a down clue, so clues like it are downs

explanation.surface: A setter says awkward vertical clues will feel fine once you have worked at them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'clues like this' refers to the clue itself, a down clue in the grid.
explanation.definitionFit: Massages given to athletes after training soothe tired muscles, so they feel good afterwards.

clue.text: Promising support, promises to support it

indicators.note: in a down clue, to support it means the promises are placed beneath the word it

parts.note: a prop is a support
IOUs are written promises to pay

explanation.surface: Pledges of backing look encouraging when they hold something up.
explanation.definitionFit: A favourable or auspicious moment is one that looks promising, a straight synonym.

clue.text: Sob quietly to put on weight? One must be cracked

parts.note: to sob is to cry
P is the musical abbreviation for piano, quietly
a gram is a unit of weight

explanation.surface: Someone weeps softly at the thought of gaining weight, as though a person must break down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put on' is a link word, also playing on gaining weight.
explanation.definitionFit: A coded message has to be broken by the recipient or codebreaker before it can be read.

clue.text: Show anger with ornament ratings here

parts.note: to lower (also spelt lour) is to frown or scowl
to deck is to adorn or ornament, as in 'deck the halls'

explanation.surface: Someone frowns at a decoration while judging scores.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ratings' are not scores but naval sailors below officer rank; 'with' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: In the Royal Navy, the non-commissioned sailors are collectively known by the name of their quarters.

clue.text: Plot with king's knight welcoming long warning to swordsmen

indicators.note: welcoming means the two chess letters take the other pieces in between them

parts.note: K is the chess abbreviation for king
N is the chess abbreviation for knight
to long for something is to itch for it
en garde is the fencer's call to take guard

explanation.surface: A conspiracy in which a king's knight shelters a fencer's drawn-out cry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Plot' looks like a scheme but means a piece of ground.
explanation.definitionFit: A plot of ground where vegetables and herbs are grown for the household's cooking.

clue.text: A bit like Balmoral's hot stuff?

parts.note: a Balmoral is a type of laced boot
the suffix -y means somewhat like, as in a bit like

explanation.surface: A query whether the royal Scottish castle is something rather sexy.
explanation.walkthrough: BALMORAL is the Royal Family's Scottish castle, but also a laced boot; 'hot' means stolen.
explanation.definitionFit: Plunder or loot is stolen property, and stolen goods are called hot.

clue.text: Campaigner's initial boost when running

indicators.note: running suggests the letters are set in motion and rearranged

explanation.surface: A political candidate gets an early lift once the race is under way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'running' suggests an election race; the 's is a link word, 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who campaigns to abolish something, historically slavery, is a reforming activist.

clue.text: Lingering impression it's time Farage is off

indicators.note: off means the letters of time Farage are disturbed and rearranged

explanation.surface: Nigel Farage's departure is overdue, yet he leaves a lasting mark.
explanation.walkthrough: Nigel Farage is a British Brexit-campaigning politician; 'it's' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: A visual image that persists briefly after the eye has looked away from the stimulus.

clue.text: Lady Chatterley's Lover, say, in some long grass, of course?

definitions.meaning: the gamekeeper Mellors is an example of a lower-class sexual partner
on a golf course the uncut long grass is the rough, and a piece of it

explanation.surface: A literary lover pictured lying in the long grass of a golf course.
explanation.walkthrough: In D. H. Lawrence's novel, the aristocratic heroine's lover is her gamekeeper; 'of course' signals golf.
explanation.definitionFit: British slang for a working-class lover, and literally a patch of golf's rough.

clue.text: Fellow on edge may do so

parts.note: a lip is an edge or rim

explanation.surface: A man perched on a ledge may topple over.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on edge' reads as nervous: someone tense may lose their temper. 'on' is a link word placing the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: To lose one's temper suddenly is something a person on edge might do.

clue.text: Rash from a French ruler unlike Louis le Gros?

parts.note: un is the French for a
Louis VI was called le Gros, the Fat, so unlike him is slim
a king is a ruler

explanation.surface: A spot of skin trouble on a French monarch, quite unlike the stout Louis.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rash' looks like a skin complaint but is the adjective 'hasty'.
explanation.definitionFit: Acting without thought or consideration is reckless and hasty.

clue.text: Dividing is thus splitting numbers up

indicators.note: up in a down clue means the whole is read from bottom to top
splitting means the pieces is and thus break the abbreviation in two

parts.note: sic is Latin for thus

explanation.surface: Splitting figures is how one divides.
explanation.walkthrough: 'splitting' places the two short words inside the abbreviation, giving NOISSICS, which 'up' turns round; 'numbers up' looks like a phrase but splits across two jobs.
explanation.definitionFit: The act of cutting or splitting apart, a formal noun matching the gerund.

clue.text: Expelling or striking guards

indicators.note: guards means the word for striking surrounds or keeps the word or

parts.note: excising means striking out or cutting away

explanation.surface: Throwing people out, or hitting the security staff.
explanation.walkthrough: 'guards' looks like a noun but is the containment verb.
explanation.definitionFit: Driving out evil spirits from a person or place is casting them out.

clue.text: He leaves Trojan woman in island

indicators.note: leaves means the word he departs from the name

parts.note: Hecuba was the queen of Troy, wife of Priam

explanation.surface: A man walks out on a woman from Troy on an island.
explanation.definitionFit: The largest Caribbean island and a country, lying south of Florida.

clue.text: Draw back and head of lion seized by bird

indicators.note: seized by means the letter is gripped inside the word for bird

parts.note: a finch is a small songbird

indicators.note: head of picks the first letter of lion

explanation.surface: Recoiling as a lion's head is grabbed by a bird.
explanation.definitionFit: To recoil or shrink away suddenly in fear or pain.

clue.text: Setter with Observer: all new and very puzzling

parts.note: the setter refers to himself as I

indicators.note: new means the letters of observer and all are formed afresh

explanation.surface: The puzzle setter works with The Observer newspaper, and everything is fresh and baffling.
explanation.walkthrough: The Observer is a British Sunday newspaper, sister to The Guardian.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that cannot be solved or settled is utterly baffling.

clue.text: Stuff from down under is alcohol

indicators.note: in a down clue, from down under means reading upward from the bottom

parts.note: to stuff is to cram

explanation.surface: Some Australian stuff is booze.
explanation.walkthrough: 'down under' suggests Australia, but means read from the bottom up.
explanation.definitionFit: A brandy distilled from grape skins and pulp left after winemaking.

clue.text: Lake by that ancient French city

parts.note: L is the map abbreviation for lake
yon is an archaic word for that

explanation.surface: A lake beside an old city in France.
explanation.definitionFit: The major city at the confluence of the Rhône and Saône in France.

clue.text: Pulse of a police officer touring this country

indicators.note: touring means the officer goes round the country

parts.note: DI is a detective inspector
the UK, from the British setter's viewpoint

explanation.surface: The heartbeat of a detective travelling around Britain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pulse' looks like a heartbeat but is an edible seed.
explanation.definitionFit: A small red bean, a legume, belonging to the family of edible seeds.

clue.text: Tender, say — moving or not!

indicators.note: moving means the letters of tender say are shifted around

explanation.surface: A tender declaration might be touching, or perhaps not.
explanation.walkthrough: 'moving' serves both as the anagram signal and inside the definition 'moving or not', read as 'not moving'.
explanation.definitionFit: Sitting down most of the time means staying put and taking little exercise.

clue.text: Online version of Macbeth is a gas

parts.note: E- as in e-book or email marks an online version
Macbeth was Thane of Glamis and Cawdor, a Scottish nobleman

explanation.surface: A web adaptation of the Scottish play is great fun.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a gas' looks like 'a laugh', but means a gas chemically; 'of' and 'is' are links.
explanation.definitionFit: A colourless hydrocarbon, a component of natural gas.

clue.text: American behind bars perhaps shot

definitions.meaning: the can is US slang for prison, so someone in it is jailed
film footage that is complete is said to be ready, filmed

explanation.surface: An American prisoner, possibly shot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shot' is film-making slang, not gunfire.
explanation.definitionFit: A film scene recorded and finished is complete, while US slang for jail is the can.
